_: The numbers a pool table runs on — one file. build.py hands the list to /billiards as D.constants, which the lab's physics reads, and renders the table on the numbers tab (and the Ninety-Degree Rule table on /equations) from the same list, so the lab and the table cannot disagree on a value. Values marked engine are pool-sauce-engine/poolsauce/constants.py; the rest say where they come from. display is what a reader sees; value is what the sim uses.

sources.model: — a modelling choice, not a measurement

constants.name: Ball radius R
constants.note: A 2¼-inch ball. Snooker's are 52.5 mm; carom 61.5 mm.

constants.name: Ball mass m
constants.note: Phenolic resin; matched to a gram in a set.

constants.name: Gravity g
constants.note: Standard gravity. The cloth slows a ball at μ_s·g while it slides and μ_r·g once it rolls.

constants.name: Ball–ball restitution e
constants.note: So a stun stop shot still creeps forward — a touch of draw fixes it.

constants.name: Ball–ball friction μ
constants.note: Alciatore's fit, μ = 0.01 + 0.108·e^(−1.088·v) with v the surface slip in m/s. Clean balls; chalk on the contact point can double it.

constants.name: Cloth sliding friction μ_s
constants.note: Worsted tournament cloth; napped cloth is higher.

constants.name: Cloth rolling resistance μ_r
constants.note: A ball at 1 m/s runs about 2 m. The 0.01 often quoted gives 5 m and ten seconds of it, which no table does.

constants.name: Cloth spinning friction
constants.note: Torque on a ball spinning in place about a vertical axis.

constants.name: Cushion efficiency
constants.note: Rubber; varies table to table and with speed. Test before a match. The soft limit — see the two rows below.

constants.name: Cushion deadening with pace
constants.note: v is the speed into the rail. The rubber gives less back the harder it is hit; the engine's √0.75 is what a soft touch gets.

constants.name: Cushion restitution floor
constants.note: Where the deadening stops — about what a break shot gets back from a rail.

constants.name: Cushion friction μ_c
constants.note: How much of the side spin the rail takes hold of; running side shortens the angle, reverse widens it.

constants.name: 9-ft playing surface
constants.note: Inside the cushion noses; a 7-ft bar table is 1.98 × 0.99 m.

constants.name: Pocket mouth
constants.note: Corner spec; the lab drops a ball whose centre crosses the mouth — a capture radius of half the mouth, 0.0572 m, on the ball's centre.

constants.name: Pocket shelf
constants.note: Typicals, a variable per pocket; a ball at the mouth needs that much roll left to fall, or it hangs.

constants.name: Squirt
constants.display: 5° per unit of side — 2.5° at full side
constants.note: A cue constant, not a table one; a low-deflection shaft roughly halves it.

constants.name: Swerve
constants.enters: the curve back while the ball slides
constants.note: Lateral g-fraction at full side, from the cue's slight natural elevation.
